text_blocks.snippet: Arthritis in the foot can cause a range of symptoms, most commonly including joint pain, stiffness, and swelling. These symptoms can make it difficult to walk, stand, or put weight on the affected foot. Other potential symptoms include tenderness to the touch, skin discoloration, a feeling of warmth around the joint, and a reduced range of motion.

list.snippet: Joint Pain: Pain can be deep and aching, or sharp and stabbing, and may worsen with activity or improve with rest.
Stiffness: Joints may feel stiff, especially in the morning or after periods of rest.
Swelling: The affected joints may appear swollen and feel warm to the touch.
Reduced Range of Motion: Difficulty bending or moving the foot and ankle through their full range of motion.
Tenderness: The affected joints may be tender to the touch.
Skin Discoloration/Warmth: The skin around the affected joint may appear discolored or feel warm.
